title: A Orbit for the Terminal
premise: Coral Okonkwo, a clone of the murdered detective whose cold case he inherited, tends a lonely beacon at the system's edge—until a nine-second gravity flicker reveals the beacon is actually broadcasting a forged ceasefire signal keeping two hostile fleets apart. As both fleets converge to investigate the anomaly, Coral must decide whether to preserve the lie that prevents war or expose the truth about his original's murder, which was committed by the very admiral who built the deception. In the end, Coral broadcasts the original's final testimony and lets the fleets choose peace for themselves, sacrificing the beacon—and nearly himself—to end the lie forever.
about_author: Casper Crane is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years maintaining automated relay stations in deep space. Their fiction explores what it means to inherit a life you never chose.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He maintains the beacon alone, logging routine transmissions and rereading his original's unsolved murder file as a private ritual. A supply ship drops off a stranger's message addressed to 'Detective Okonkwo'—the first mail he's received in years. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; instruments fail, then recover. Coral discovers the beacon's core is transmitting an encrypted signal far more powerful than its design allows—a forged fleet-wide ceasefire order timestamped the day his original died. Emotional beat: vertigo of realizing his whole life sits atop a secret.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Coral and journal entries from the original Okonkwo. The journals reveal the detective discovered the ceasefire was fake before his death and hid evidence inside the beacon itself. Coral realizes someone killed to protect the lie. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Fleet officer Imani Voss's POV aboard the Concordance flagship. The gravity flicker has made both fleets suspicious; her admiral orders a course toward the beacon. Voss suspects the armistice they've all obeyed for years rests on nothing. Emotional beat: institutional loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. An advance scout arrives claiming to be a maintenance inspector but is clearly hunting something. Coral plays dumb, hides the original's journals inside the beacon's coolant housing, and narrowly survives an inspection. Emotional beat: fear teaching him how good a liar he can be.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Reading deeper into the journals, Coral learns he wasn't commissioned by any agency—he was grown by the original himself, deliberately, to finish the case if the detective failed. His identity crisis peaks: is he a person or a dead man's contingency plan? Emotional beat: rage transforming into resolve.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Both fleets arrive in orbit around the beacon station under mutual pretense of 'joint investigation.' Voss meets Coral and recognizes the family resemblance to photos of the dead detective. She says nothing—but she knows. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Confession
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax begins. The admiral who ordered the original's murder arrives personally to erase the beacon. Coral triggers the hidden evidence: the original's recorded testimony naming the admiral, broadcast on open channels to both fleets. The admiral orders the station destroyed. Emotional beat: terror and triumph entwined.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds Again
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. As the station burns, Coral manually holds the true ceasefire—not a forgery this time, but the original's dying plea for peace—transmitting while the gravity flicker returns, stalling both fleets' weapons systems for nine critical seconds. Voss defies orders and shields the station with her ship. Emotional beat: sacrifice without certainty.

chapters.title: A Orbit for the Terminal
chapters.summary: Epilogue, split between Coral recovering aboard Voss's ship and the fleets negotiating in earnest. The lie is dead; the truth survived. Coral, no longer invisible and no longer merely a copy, chooses his own name and stays on as witness to the talks. Emotional beat: identity claimed, not inherited.
